clue.text: Ape eats small reptile and big, reflecting bigger world

indicators.note: a word that eats something takes it inside, so the ape synonym goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to ape is to mimic
a croc is the shortened, small form of crocodile
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, a big size

explanation.surface: A monkey devours a little reptile and something large, in a picture of the wider world.
explanation.definitionFit: Something microcosmic is a miniature that mirrors a larger world or system in small.

clue.text: Get confused by playwright in assessing growing business

indicators.note: the word in tells us the combined pieces sit inside the assessing synonym

parts.note: assessing work, as a teacher does, is marking it

indicators.note: confused means the letters of get are jumbled

parts.note: John Arden is an English playwright

explanation.surface: Someone is muddled by a dramatist while evaluating a horticultural company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link; 'confused' rearranges the clue's own word, and the inserted run sits after the K of the assessing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Market gardening is the business of raising vegetables and fruit for sale, so it is literally growing produce commercially.

clue.text: Cuisine's hotter if lots is initially applied

definitions.text: Cuisine's hotter if lots is initially applied

indicators.note: initially means we take the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A cook observes that food gets spicier when plenty of something is added.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the hot pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding plenty of chilli pepper makes a dish hotter, so the clue as a whole describes this spice.

clue.text: Mineral to go round an aromatic plant

parts.note: ore is mineral-bearing rock

indicators.note: round says the go synonym is placed around the little word an

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock seems to travel around a fragrant herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a fragrant herb of the mint family used in cooking, an example of an aromatic plant.

clue.text: Bans spouse's family? Quite the contrary!

indicators.note: says to swap a word for its opposite, here the in at the front of the relatives' term turns to its counterpart

parts.note: your husband's or wife's relatives are your in-laws

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they are barring their partner's relatives, then insists the reverse is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the contrary' swaps IN in INLAWS for its opposite, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw something is to forbid it, so the verb form matches bans as a synonym.

clue.text: Post held in South Africa, once a principal means of propulsion

definitions.text: once a principal means of propulsion

indicators.note: held means the pieces are kept inside the post synonym

parts.note: the post is the mail
taken as written

explanation.surface: A job is kept in South Africa, apparently formerly the leading way of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' belongs to the definition: sailing ships were formerly the main way to travel by sea, so the sail no longer is.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainsail was the chief sail driving a sailing ship, historically the principal power for vessels.

clue.text: "Religious instruction in state" — Czech Republic's leader makes a promise to the people

indicators.note: makes signals that the gathered letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a British school subject
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word republic

explanation.surface: A headline about Czech politics: the country's head pledges religious teaching in schools to its citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges RI, INSTATE, CZECH and R together. The Citizen's Charter was a 1991 UK government initiative setting out what the public could expect from services.
explanation.definitionFit: The Citizen's Charter was a British government pledge of standards for public services, a promise made to the people.

clue.text: A pretty female involved in scandal

indicators.note: involved means the female abbreviation is taken in with the pretty synonym

parts.note: fair means pretty, good-looking

explanation.surface: An attractive woman is caught up in a public scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a scandalous or notorious event, often a love affair that becomes public.

clue.text: Order many soldiers into the river

indicators.note: into says the pieces go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another between England and Wales
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

explanation.surface: An officer commands a large troop to march into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order issued by an authority.

clue.text: Turn right in 5, being surreptitious

indicators.note: in tells us the turn and right pieces sit within the number

parts.note: the figure 5 written as a word is five
a U-turn is a turn, so U can stand for it

explanation.surface: Directions to turn right at five, being sneaky about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 looks like a reference to clue 5, but it is simply the number FIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Furtive and surreptitious are synonyms, both describing secretive behaviour meant to avoid notice.

clue.text: Is Scotland's heart in the national emblem?

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces go inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A question about whether Scotland's core lies within its national symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOTLAND has eight letters, so its heart is TL.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is the national emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: New World features in new Carmen aria right away

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement
away says the abbreviation for right is removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: An American theme turns up in a fresh version of an operatic Carmen song with its right removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one R out of CARMENARIA and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are artefacts and features characteristic of American culture; America was called the New World.

clue.text: Czarist's heart goes out to assisted scholar

indicators.note: goes out suggests the core letters are scattered and rearranged
the heart of the word means all but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Russian royalist's sympathy is extended to a needy student.
explanation.walkthrough: CZARIST minus its first and last letters is ZARIS, which 'goes out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A sizar is a student at Cambridge or Dublin who received financial help from the college, so an assisted scholar.

clue.text: Take time for fad

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, used on prescriptions
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to take one's time over a passing craze.
explanation.definitionFit: A rage is a craze, as in 'all the rage', so it means a fad.

clue.text: Sense of guilt once scenic redevelopment occurs

indicators.note: a redevelopment rebuilds something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guilty feeling arises once a beautiful landscape is built over.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscience is the inner sense of right and wrong that produces feelings of guilt.

clue.text: Look back into unfinished class of sweet

indicators.note: into means the reversed piece goes inside the trimmed class word
unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a seminar is a teaching class

indicators.note: back means the look synonym is read in reverse

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone glances back into an incomplete lesson about desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives OL; 'unfinished' trims the class word to SEMINA. In Britain a sweet is a dessert course, not just a candy.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is made into a milk pudding, so in British usage it is a sweet, a dessert.

clue.text: Proportion of the aristocracy losing energy and receiving money

indicators.note: receiving means the money piece is taken inside
losing means a letter is dropped

parts.note: the peerage is the body of nobles
E is the physics symbol for energy
a cent is a coin, money

explanation.surface: A share of the nobility lose their vigour while getting cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' leaves PERAGE, which 'receiving' then opens up for the coin. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A percentage is a proportion expressed as parts per hundred.

clue.text: Preserve from an embarrassing situation

definitions.meaning: to preserve food in vinegar or brine
a tricky fix or awkward plight

explanation.surface: Someone protects themselves from an awkward predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickle means both to preserve in brine and, colloquially, a predicament or mess.

clue.text: Half-exposed, like Ilium's towers

definitions.meaning: with the upper half of the body bare
Marlowe wrote of 'the ... towers of Ilium', meaning towers so tall their tops could not be seen

explanation.walkthrough: Ilium is Troy; the line comes from Marlowe's Doctor Faustus about Helen of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means bare-breasted and, in Marlowe's sense, immeasurably tall.

clue.text: Astronomer, one in ship mostly

indicators.note: in means the one piece goes inside the shortened ship
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a galleon is a large old sailing ship
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A stargazer is a passenger on a vessel, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts GALLEON to GALLEO, and I goes between its two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer who championed the heliocentric model.

clue.text: A lot of old money for a missile

indicators.note: a lot of but not all, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: the scudo was an old Italian silver coin

explanation.surface: A lot of old cash is spent on a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scud is a Soviet-designed ballistic missile.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scud is a type of ballistic missile, famous from the Gulf War.

clue.text: Padre's syllogism is somewhat ostentatious

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chaplain's logical argument is rather showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothes are smart and showy, so the word can mean ostentatious.

clue.text: About to repeat operation in faith

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to redo is to perform an operation again

explanation.surface: A surgeon is about to repeat an operation, trusting in faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of belief, a creed or faith.

clue.text: Count on friends being serious

parts.note: pals are friends
grave means serious

explanation.surface: Relying on one's companions is a solemn matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A palsgrave was a count palatine, a German nobleman of that rank.

clue.text: Rise in costume

definitions.meaning: to get out of bed or stand up
an outfit, often an elaborate one

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means to rise; as a noun it means an outfit.

clue.text: Take no action about multinational that's open to the public

indicators.note: about means the lazing word goes round the company

parts.note: to laze is to idle, doing nothing
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a British multinational company

explanation.surface: Idling around a big company that welcomes visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To laicize is to make lay or secular, removing clerical control so something is open to all.

clue.text: For example: less than honest statements about drink that isn't large?

definitions.text: For example: less than honest statements about drink that isn't large?

indicators.note: about means the lies go round the drink

parts.note: untruthful statements are lies
a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone tells fibs about a small drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than honest' is itself understatement for dishonest, so the clue is its own example of the figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negating the opposite, like saying less than honest to mean lying.

clue.text: Fat French consumer, a chirpy character

parts.note: gras is French for fat
a shopper is a consumer

explanation.surface: A plump French customer is a cheerful sort.
explanation.definitionFit: The grasshopper chirps by rubbing its legs, so it is a chirpy character in a punning sense.
